changes: LLMProviderRow, RelayProviderRow and ServerApiKeyField now share useServerCredentials for status reads, legacy browser-key cleanup, verified saves/removals, read retry and the existing useModelOperation lifecycle. Duplicate configured/saved flags, success timers and the obsolete relay cleanup wrapper are deleted.

Provider and relay editors remount on account/role identity changes; provider identity includes the provider and server key. Pending results cannot update the replacement editor or trigger relay catalog refresh after cleanup.

Relay URL-only writes omit an empty API-key draft and preserve stored credentials. Confirmed removals clear both backend relay fields and the non-secret browser URL cache. Drafts remain on failure and inputs are locked during writes.

SystemService exposes one complete SystemStats read. Tauri combines cached native metadata with native live values; a failed native sample falls back to a complete authenticated server snapshot. It no longer merges hardware facts from one computer with live statistics from another.

The old browser/Electron placeholder responses, live/server projection methods, unused frontend live-temperature shape and all-zero failure snapshot are removed. Invalid samples throw; genuine zero CPU load, GPU utilization and uptime remain valid.

Kernel monitor stores one confirmed snapshot and history, identifies local versus server host, and clears stale statistics/history on failure. Sampling is scheduled two seconds after settlement instead of overlapping fixed intervals, with a ten-second request signal, account cleanup and no late rendering.
History is reset when the source or hostname changes. Computer exploration remains mounted when telemetry fails.
validationNotes: Ten cases added to existing tests: four provider/relay mutation and failure/account scenarios, two browser/Electron error-contract cases, native coherent sampling/fallback, stalled-native cancellation, monitor slow/failure/recovery lifecycle and monitor account isolation.

Credential behavior uses extracted production UI functions/hooks and real settingsKeys/apiClient over synthetic fetch; disclosure chrome/buttons/icons are substitutes. Existing provider-model tests continue to cover model drafts and cancelled connection probes.

Telemetry service tests import the actual SystemService with mocked API transport and native invoke. Monitor tests execute actual production functions with synthetic widgets/clock. The existing backend system-stat test also samples the real host; no native GUI was driven.

Initial validation exposed an old test holding a detached input after an account remount, a test-only inferred-map typing error, and JSX in a .ts test. These fixtures were corrected; they are not counted as production defect fixes.
Final validation fingerprints cover all six changed files and preserve the most recent prune40-64 baselines.
limitations: Native IPC does not provide cancellation of an already-running OS query. The signal ends frontend waiting, removes its listener and suppresses fallback/late rendering; it cannot undo native work already started.

Native metadata is cached while native reads succeed and invalidated after a native failure. Server fallback is identified as the Lumi server host; no claim is made that a remotely connected backend is the client computer.
The native IPC import itself has no cancellation protocol. Native calls and backend reads are bounded by the supplied signal after import; actual native hardware timing was not benchmarked.

Credential storage remains the existing machine-wide backend contract, with per-editor serialization only. A frontend abort cannot undo a backend-accepted write. The non-secret relay URL still uses its existing browser cache for the editor initial value.
Business code decreases by 158 lines; tests grow by 113; the total decreases by 45. No new business/test file or replacement subsystem was created.
No full-suite run, external model/provider call, real credential update, native-client acceptance, backend rebuild, commit, push or client restart.
